knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. It's a way for code to be integrated in
chunks which offers the organization of running individual code throughout the file without running the entire file all together.

The package I chose to utilize is called "f1dataR" which is a public data-set I found from GitHub https://github.com/SCasanova/f1dataR.git 
The data-set is filled with data along the lines of Formula 1 racing drivers and their racing output each week. The variables used in the data-set are
"driver_id", "constructor_id" "points", "position", "grid", "laps", "status", "gap","fastest_rank", "fastest", "top_speed_kph" and "time_sec" just to
get an idea of what collection consists of. 

Below are the packages and library call I called for this document.


```{r f1dataR}
library(f1dataR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```


Now that we have our packages selected and current, we will use "load_results()" to pull from the "f1dataR" data. Below you will see the we have pulled
the most "current"/"2026" season and "last"/"20" round that was raced. This function also allows for the function to utilized like the example I will display
here = <f1 <-load_results(season = "current", round = "last")> which accepts characters or numeric input. This code would call for the most current racing results
from the last known race. We then called for the head() and names() of the "f1" matrix to get a glimpse of the attached variables.



```{r data-pull}
f1 <-load_results(season = "2026", round = "20")
head(f1)
names(f1)
```


During this time, the Formula 1 organization raced at the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which is what our example will consist of data wise. The code chunk
below is a LaTeX math expression that calculates the net positions gained during the race. In other words, the starting position compared to the final position
in the race for each driver. For example, Max Verstappen started on the "grid" in the 21st position. He then finished in the 2nd "position" in the race.
This resulted in a gain of 19 positions which is displayed under the "delta_p" variable. 


```{r LaTeX}
f1_results <- load_results(season = "current", round = "last") %>%
  mutate(
    grid = as.numeric(grid),
    position = as.numeric(position),
    delta_p = grid - position
  )
print(f1_results[, c("driver_id", "delta_p")])
```



Below, we've combined the "f1" data-set with the column "points" and we plot them in conjunction with "driver_id" to produce a scatter-plot using "geom_point()."
The variable "points" is stored as a character in the data-set, so we use the "as.numeric" function to convert the values as numbers rather than characters
to be plotted. The plot uses "driver_id" as our x-axis and "points" as our y-axis to display the amount of points each driver did, or did not collect during this race.


```{r f1 plot}
f1$points <- as.numeric(f1$points)

ggplot(f1, aes(x = driver_id, y = points)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) + 
  labs(title = "F1 Points by Driver", x = "Driver ID", y = "Points")
```


Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
